name: Porter's Five Forces
summary: Industry attractiveness = the combined pressure of rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, buyer power and supplier power. Useful inside market entry and M&A market assessments.
opening_line: To judge how attractive this industry is, I'd look at rivalry, entry barriers, substitutes, and the bargaining power of buyers and suppliers.
when_to_use: Assessing industry attractiveness or profitability potential
The 'market' branch of market entry, M&A or investment cases
when_not_to_use: As a whole case structure: interviewers see it as generic. Use it inside a bucket

buckets.name: Rivalry
questions: How concentrated? Growth rate? Price competition?

buckets.name: Entry & substitutes
questions: Capital, regulatory or brand barriers? Alternatives customers could switch to?

buckets.name: Buyers & suppliers
questions: Are customers or suppliers concentrated? Switching costs?

industry_adaptations.note: Classic low-attractiveness industry: high rivalry, powerful suppliers (Boeing/Airbus, labour), commoditised product.

common_mistakes: Using it as the entire framework
Listing forces without concluding what they mean for the client
